title: Prepositions of Behaviour: to, on, about

vocabulary.example: His behaviour in class is very good.

vocabulary.meaning_en: words that are often used together
very unkind to someone, making them suffer

vocabulary.example: She is always kind to her neighbours.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not polite to someone; showing no respect
vocabulary.example: Don't be rude to the waiter.
The teacher was very helpful to her students.

vocabulary.meaning_en: strict and demanding with someone (often to make them better)
vocabulary.example: My coach was tough on me so I could be the best.

vocabulary.meaning_en: gentle and not strict with someone
vocabulary.example: Go easy on him; it's his first day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: unpleasant and unkind to someone; hard and unpleasant
vocabulary.example: The manager was rough on the new workers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: thinking only about yourself in a situation
vocabulary.example: Don't be selfish about the food; share it.

vocabulary.note_ar: not crazy about = لا يحبه كثيرًا
vocabulary.note_en: Not crazy about = don't like it much.
vocabulary.example: I'm crazy about my new car.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not nice in the way you do something
vocabulary.note_en: Mean also has another meaning: to signify.
vocabulary.example: He was mean about lending me money.

vocabulary.meaning_en: too strict with yourself; criticising yourself too much
vocabulary.example: Don't be so hard on yourself. Everyone makes mistakes.

fine_lines.title: tough on vs rough on
fine_lines.explanation_ar: tough on = صارم ويُصعّب الأمور لكن غالبًا لهدف جيد (ليجعلك أقوى). rough on = قاسٍ وغير لطيف، ولا شيء جيد فيه.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Tough on = strict, makes things difficult, often for a good reason (to make you stronger). Rough on = unpleasant and unkind; nothing good about it.

examples.sentence: My teachers were tough on me because they wanted me to do well.
That guard was rough on the visitors. It wasn't fair.

fine_lines.title: crazy vs crazy about
fine_lines.explanation_ar: crazy وحدها = مجنون. crazy about something = أحبه كثيرًا جدًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Crazy alone = mad, not normal. Crazy about something = love it very much.

examples.sentence: My son is crazy about football.

fine_lines.title: to vs on vs about (with adjectives)
fine_lines.explanation_ar: to = اتجاه: السلوك يذهب نحو شخص (kind to). on = على السطح: السلوك يُوضع على الشخص فيشعر به (tough on). about = حول الموضوع (selfish about).
fine_lines.explanation_en: to = direction: the behaviour goes to a person (kind to). on = on the surface: the behaviour is put on the person and they feel it (tough on). about = around a subject (selfish about).

examples.sentence: She is easy on her kids.
He was kind about helping the old lady.

expressions.phrase: Don't be so hard on yourself.
expressions.example: You only made one mistake. Don't be so hard on yourself.

expressions.meaning_en: Don't be too strict with him.
expressions.example: He's new here. Go easy on him.

expressions.meaning_en: being strict with someone because you care about them
expressions.example: My father gave me tough love, and it helped me.

grammar.title: Adjective + preposition to describe behaviour
grammar.explanation_ar: حروف الجر تُستخدم عادة للاتجاه والزمن والسبب، لكن عندما نضعها بعد صفة نصف بها كيف يتصرف شخص ما. التركيب: الفاعل + be + صفة + حرف جر + شخص/شيء.
grammar.explanation_en: Prepositions usually show direction, time and reason, but after an adjective they describe how someone behaves. Structure: subject + be + adjective + preposition + person/thing.
examples: He is cruel to his dog.
My parents were easy on me.
She was selfish about the food.

grammar.title: Adjective + to (direction)
grammar.explanation_ar: to تعني الاتجاه: السلوك يتجه نحو شخص. cruel to, kind to, rude to, helpful to.
grammar.explanation_en: To shows direction: the behaviour goes toward a person. cruel to, kind to, rude to, helpful to.
examples: Be kind to your little brother.
The guide was very helpful to us.

grammar.title: Adjective + on (put on someone)
grammar.explanation_ar: on تعني أن السلوك يقع على الشخص فيشعر به: tough on, easy on, rough on, hard on.
grammar.explanation_en: On means the behaviour is put on the person; they feel it: tough on, easy on, rough on, hard on.
examples: The new law is tough on crime.
The exam was rough on me.

grammar.title: Adjective + about (the subject)
grammar.explanation_ar: about تعني حول موضوع أو شيء: selfish about, crazy about, mean about, kind about.
grammar.explanation_en: About means around a subject or thing: selfish about, crazy about, mean about, kind about.
examples: She was mean about sharing her notes.

questions.question: My coach was ___ me so I could be the best.
questions.explanation_en: Strict for a good reason: tough on.

questions.question: The teacher was very ___ her students, so they loved her.
"I'm crazy about this restaurant." means ___.
questions.explanation_en: Crazy about = love it very much.

questions.question: She was ___ the dog, so they took it away from her.
"Rough on" is different from "tough on" because rough on is ___.
"Go easy on him" means ___.
choices: Don't be too strict with him.
questions.explanation_en: Don't be too strict with him.

questions.question: "Don't be so hard on yourself" means ___.
